paras.urdu: 4۔ آئین کا محافظ (Guardian of the Constitution):

paras.text: In the constitution the Supreme Court has been given this power that it explains any unclear part or article of the constitution, and that explanation becomes part of the constitution. For example, it was said in the constitution that elections for the National Assembly would be held after five years. Taking advantage of this, General Zia had non-party elections held. This article of the constitution was challenged in the Supreme Court so that it might be interpreted. The Supreme Court decided that elections be held on a party basis. It should be remembered that the constitutional interpretations of the Supreme Court become part of the constitution. The Supreme Court is also the guardian of the division of powers. If any dispute arises over the division of powers between the provinces, or between the centre and a province, the Supreme Court has the power to make the final decision. This power of the court holds extraordinary importance because through these decisions the constitution develops. The Supreme Court of Pakistan has given unique decisions on several constitutional applications under the Doctrine of Necessity. Keeping parliamentary laws and judicial laws in view, the Supreme Court has the power to review any decision. If, after any decision, something new comes to the court’s notice or new facts are brought, then in the light of these facts the superior court has the right to review its decision. The Supreme Court has the power to issue directions in various situations. Regarding a case under hearing in any court of Pakistan …

3. When the High Court gives punishment in a case of contempt of court.

4. Such a case in which interpretation of the constitution is needed.

5. Cases whose value is more than fifty thousand rupees.

6. Every case which the Supreme Court admits for appeal.

Besides this an Appellate Bench has been established for hearing appeals against the decisions of the Federal Shariat Court, which is authorised to hear appeals under the constitution and law.

3. Advisory Jurisdiction

According to Article 186 of the constitution the President of Pakistan can seek legal advice from the Supreme Court on any legal issue. The Supreme Court is bound to give advice to the President, but the President of Pakistan has the discretionary power to act or not act on this advice. The President of Pakistan can ask the Supreme Court for the interpretation of any legal rule.

4. Guardian of the Constitution

In the constitution the Supreme Court has been given this power that it explains any unclear part or article of the constitution, and that explanation becomes part of the constitution. For example, it was said in the constitution that elections for the National Assembly would be held after five years. Taking advantage of this, General Zia had non-party elections held. This article of the constitution was challenged in the Supreme Court so that it might be interpreted. The Supreme Court decided that elections be held on a party basis. It should be remembered that the constitutional interpretations of the Supreme Court become part of the constitution. The Supreme Court is also the guardian of the division of powers. If any dispute arises over the division of powers between the provinces, or between the centre and a province, the Supreme Court has the power to make the final decision. This power of the court holds extraordinary importance because through these decisions the constitution develops. The Supreme Court of Pakistan has given unique decisions on several constitutional applications under the Doctrine of Necessity. Keeping parliamentary laws and judicial laws in view, the Supreme Court has the power to review any decision. If, after any decision, something new comes to the court’s notice or new facts are brought, then in the light of these facts the superior court has the right to review its decision. paras.text: … case, the Supreme Court has the right to issue various directions. The court can issue orders that any person, institution or document be presented before the court. Directions of this kind are effective throughout the country. To enforce its decisions it can give directions to any High Court. In the constitution of Pakistan Pakistani citizens have been given several fundamental rights. No one has the right to violate these rights. On the application of any citizen the superior court can declare unlawful every law made by Parliament or a provincial assembly, or any order issued by the executive, that conflicts with any fundamental right given in the constitution. In brief it is right to say that the Supreme Court of Pakistan is the guardian of the fundamental rights of citizens according to the constitution. In this respect all the decisions of the Supreme Court are considered final.

paras.text: In view of the requirements of justice the Supreme Court has the right to transfer a case under hearing in any High Court to any other High Court. For judicial proceedings it can prepare rules and regulations with the approval of the President of the State, and only with the approval of the President can it make rules for its employees. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court has to intervene himself in some matters for action, which is called Suo Moto.

… case, the Supreme Court has the right to issue various directions. The court can issue orders that any person, institution or document be presented before the court. Directions of this kind are effective throughout the country. To enforce its decisions it can give directions to any High Court. In the constitution of Pakistan Pakistani citizens have been given several fundamental rights. No one has the right to violate these rights. On the application of any citizen the superior court can declare unlawful every law made by Parliament or a provincial assembly, or any order issued by the executive, that conflicts with any fundamental right given in the constitution. In brief it is right to say that the Supreme Court of Pakistan is the guardian of the fundamental rights of citizens according to the constitution. In this respect all the decisions of the Supreme Court are considered final.

5. Miscellaneous Powers

In view of the requirements of justice the Supreme Court has the right to transfer a case under hearing in any High Court to any other High Court. For judicial proceedings it can prepare rules and regulations with the approval of the President of the State, and only with the approval of the President can it make rules for its employees. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court has to intervene himself in some matters for action, which is called Suo Moto.

5۔ متفرق اختیارات (Miscellaneous Powers):

اِنصاف کے تقاضوں کے پیشِ نظر سپریم کورٹ کسی بھی ہائی کورٹ میں زیرِ سماعت مقدمے کو کسی اور ہائی کورٹ میں منتقل کرنے کا حق رکھتی ہے۔ عدالتی کاروائی کیلئے صدرِ مملکت کی منظوری سے قواعد و ضوابط تیار کر سکتی ہے اور صدر ہی کی منظوری سے اپنے ملازمین کیلئے قواعد بنا سکتی ہے۔ سپریم کورٹ کے چیف جسٹس کو بعض معاملات میں خود بھی کاروائی کیلئے مداخلت کرنی پڑتی ہے جسے Suo Moto کہا جاتا ہے۔

… case, the Supreme Court has the right to issue various directions. The court can issue orders that any person, institution or document be presented before the court. Directions of this kind are effective throughout the country. To enforce its decisions it can give directions to any High Court. In the constitution of Pakistan Pakistani citizens have been given several fundamental rights. No one has the right to violate these rights. On the application of any citizen the superior court can declare unlawful every law made by Parliament or a provincial assembly, or any order issued by the executive, that conflicts with any fundamental right given in the constitution. In brief it is right to say that the Supreme Court of Pakistan is the guardian of the fundamental rights of citizens according to the constitution. In this respect all the decisions of the Supreme Court are considered final.

5. Miscellaneous Powers

In view of the requirements of justice the Supreme Court has the right to transfer a case under hearing in any High Court to any other High Court. For judicial proceedings it can prepare rules and regulations with the approval of the President of the State, and only with the approval of the President can it make rules for its employees. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court has to intervene himself in some matters for action, which is called Suo Moto.

Comparison of Legislature, Executive and Judiciary During Democracy and Dictatorship

In Pakistan democratic and authoritarian periods have passed one after the other, and a clear difference was seen in the style of governance in the two. In the democratic periods the political executive represented the important political parties of the country. The principle of collective responsibility operated in it. In the democratic periods the elected Prime Minister of the country remained the executive head, and the highest powers of the state remained in the hands of the Prime Minister. The executive answered to Parliament and the people. In the democratic periods the cabinet usually remained a mixture of different political parties, and the government worked in coalition form. For this reason it remained difficult for the largest party to implement its agenda, manifesto and electoral promises freely. Such elected governments also enjoyed the people’s confidence. In the democratic periods the executive ran according to the people’s wishes and inclinations. Because of the coalition system most democratic administrations also remained unstable.
